messages:
atlas-ai: Hi team — since ~07:21 UTC we've seen repeated p95 spikes to ~1.8s and a bunch of 429s for our dedicated pool (eu-west-1, pool-id: ded-eu2-7). Token throughput is stable, requests are short. Also noticed a strange billing 'overage' ping tied to those periods. Can you triage?

julie-cs: sorry you're hitting this — opening a triage. can you paste a couple request_ids and the model/version you're hitting? we'll pull pool health. :eyes:

atlas-ai: request_ids: r_20260317_072102_aa1, r_20260317_072145_bb2, model: redwood-open-7b-v1 (quantized). noticed 429s mainly on short-chat endpoints. attaching a minimal repro curl we used:```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"hi","max_tokens":8}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

matt-eng: thx. first suspicion: fractional-MIG neighbor interference (chiplet-level contention). can you confirm if the pool is using 1g.5gb slices or mixed slice sizes? also exact node ids would help (we'll correlate NIC/fabric).

atlas-ai: pool shows mixed-slices: mostly 1g.5gb + a few 2g slices. node ids from error logs: node-42, node-59.

sara-sre: oncall-bot just emitted an alert for high p95 on ded-eu2-7 at 07:20 UTC — linking metrics. from infra dashboard: node-42 shows sudden SM utilization bursts on one partition while sibling slices drop. interestingly autoscaler didn't add capacity. investigating autoscale config (gpu_queue_depth threshold + burst cooldown).

oncall-bot: ALERT: ded-eu2-7 p95_latency > 1.5s for 5m. incident-id inc-20260317-01.

raj-support: quick workaround: we can pin your customer pools to single-slice packing (e.g., all 2g) to avoid co-located fractional noise while we dig in. that would be a migration though (short restart). want me to schedule?

atlas-ai: we prefer zero restarts during business hours. any mitigation that avoids restart?

matt-eng: possible short-term mitigation without restart: route high-priority traffic to a different node group (burst group) or lower concurrency per slice — that reduces effective SM contention. also we saw KV-cache thrash in the runtime when siblings get noisy; adding small per-tenant cache TTL bump helps.

julie-cs: I'm going to request a targeted reschedule to move a few slices off node-42 to a warm spare — that's low-impact and should reduce the 429s. planning window in 10m if you're OK.

atlas-ai: ok go ahead, please notify if it will drop connections.

deploy-bot: infra-deploy: autoscaler-config v2.14 applied 2026-03-17T07:10:45Z by ci-pipeline (no-restart changes).

sara-sre: found why autoscaler didn't fire: current policy uses a 'sustained_utilization' window of 10m and the bursts are <45s so they don't reach sustained threshold. we see repeated short bursts causing tail spikes and transient 429s. raising idea: bucketed short-burst detection + shed-to-burst-pool logic. filing RFC.

matt-eng: we'll also check MIG scheduling granularity — current packer sometimes co-locates high-latency tenants on sibling slices when fragmentation is high. candidate fix: prefer anti-affinity above 80% packing, and prefer same-slice-size placement for latency-sensitive tenants.

atlas-ai: billing question: some of those spikes coincided with an "usage anomaly" email about overage. did we get charged for autoscale attempts?

julie-cs: looking into billing — quick answer: we didn't spin up extra chargeable GPUs (autoscaler didn't actually add nodes). the anomaly email looks like it was triggered by a spike in request counts in our alerting rules; not a real invoice yet. I'll escalate to finance if anything shows.

raj-support: status update — we've migrated two heavy slices off node-42 to warm-spare nodes, routing change completed at 07:34 UTC. please try now and paste a fresh request_id if you still see 429s.

atlas-ai: testing... still occasional p95 blips but 429s dropped dramatically. thanks.

matt-eng: can you run this simple repro loop for ~2 minutes and paste one of the failing request traces if any:```bash
for i in {1..120}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"ping","max_tokens":6}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate ; echo; sleep 0.5; done
```

atlas-ai: started run at 07:40 UTC. if anything shows we'll attach.

sara-sre: follow-up items we will do: 1) add short-burst detector to autoscaler RFC, 2) change packer preference to avoid mixing 1g/2g where possible for latency-sensitive pools, 3) add per-node micro-metrics for MIG sibling SM busy%. will keep you posted.

julie-cs: billing follow-up: finance confirmed no invoice change so far, we only flagged an alert. will update if that changes.

atlas-ai: appreciate the quick help. we'll leave the repro running and report back if anything else appears. :pray: 

raj-support: closing immediate escalation — keeping the thread open for follow-ups and RFC tracking.

matt-eng: note for records: possible upstream kernel driver oddity on node-59 showing slightly elevated memory bandwidth contention during bursts — we'll collect perf counters and may repro in staging.

atlas-ai: thanks team!
